clue.text: Represent, as a member, in hearing

indicators.note: in hearing means the word is taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a limb is a member of the body, such as an arm or leg

explanation.surface: Someone acts on behalf of a body, as one of its members, at a formal hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Represent' as a delegate is the false lead; limn means to depict, and it sounds the same as LIMB.
explanation.definitionFit: To limn is to depict or portray, so it is a synonym of represent in the artistic sense.

clue.text: Composer finding king hard hearted

indicators.note: hearted says the letter sits at the centre of the king's name

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's king
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A composer is found to be as cold and cruel as a hard-hearted king.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'hard-hearted'; split it so 'hard' gives H and 'hearted' puts it into LEAR. Franz Lehár wrote The Merry Widow.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Lehar was the Hungarian composer of operettas such as The Merry Widow.

clue.text: Fairest competitor in all the races

definitions.text: Fairest competitor in all the races

parts.words: Fairest competitor in all the races
parts.note: a beauty contest entrant of every race and nation, judged the fairest of all, not a runner

explanation.definitionFit: The winner of the international beauty pageant is crowned the most beautiful contestant from all nations.

clue.text: Crispbread made specially for shellfish

indicators.note: something made specially is put together afresh, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crispbread has been baked to order for seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: A spider crab is a long-legged crab, and crabs are counted as shellfish in the kitchen.

clue.text: Carrying club, gangster goes to office in church

indicators.note: goes to says the second piece follows on after the first

parts.note: a priest is a small club used by anglers to kill fish
a hood is a gangster or hoodlum

explanation.surface: An armed gangster carrying a club heads off to a church office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carrying' is a link to the surface; a priest is an angler's club, a convention many solvers will not know.
explanation.definitionFit: The priesthood is the office or rank of priest held by clergy within the church.

clue.text: Nest in tree, a few feet up

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a yard is three feet

explanation.surface: A nest sits in a tree a little way above the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The usual spelling is drey, a squirrel's nest; dray is an accepted variant.
explanation.definitionFit: A dray, more often spelt drey, is the twiggy nest a squirrel builds high in a tree.

clue.text: Smugglers on horseback who fail to get gold?

parts.note: runners are smugglers, as in gun-runners or rum-runners
a jockey who is up is mounted on the horse

explanation.surface: Mounted smugglers fail to get their hands on the gold they were after.
explanation.walkthrough: Gold is the winner's medal, not loot; the question mark flags the shift.
explanation.definitionFit: Those finishing second or lower miss out on first place and hence on the gold medal.

clue.text: Composer forming Liberal party, originally

parts.note: a rave is a large dance party

indicators.note: originally says take the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A composer goes into politics, forming the Liberal Party in its early days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal party' reads as one political name; it is two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Maurice Ravel was a French composer, best known for Bolero.

clue.text: What made Tom heard in Oxford, for example?

definitions.text: What made Tom heard in Oxford, for example?

parts.words: What made Tom heard in Oxford, for example?
parts.note: Great Tom is the big bell of Christ Church, Oxford; the alloy it is cast from is what makes it ring out

explanation.definitionFit: Bell metal is the bronze alloy of copper and tin from which large bells are cast.

clue.text: Where UN delegates go for award in America

parts.note: to go somewhere is to head to it, so go supplies the direction word
the United Nations sits in New York, abbreviated NY

explanation.surface: UN delegates head off somewhere to collect an American prize.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Where UN delegates go' as the phrase 'to NY', New York being home to the United Nations.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tony is the annual American prize for achievement in Broadway theatre.

clue.text: Pertaining to past and modern work of literature

parts.note: historical means relating to history, the past
novel means new or modern

explanation.surface: A literary work is described as both old-fashioned and up to date.
explanation.definitionFit: A historical novel is a work of fiction set in a past period.

clue.text: My word is broken, leading to bad behaviour

indicators.note: broken says the letters are smashed and reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone breaks their promise, and that leads to misconduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My word is broken' sounds like a broken promise; 'is' belongs to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowdyism is noisy, disorderly conduct, which is a kind of bad behaviour.

clue.text: Uproar produced by hospital unit strike

parts.note: hospital capacity is counted in beds
to lam is to strike or thrash

explanation.surface: A strike by a hospital department causes chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' looks like industrial action; it is a verb meaning hit. Bedlam was a London hospital for the insane, Bethlem.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedlam is a scene of noisy confusion, so it means uproar.

clue.text: On sea, true British resort

indicators.note: read as re-sort, it says to sort these letters again into a new order

explanation.surface: A genuine British seaside resort.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: Eastbourne is a resort on the Sussex coast of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Eastbourne is a seaside town on the south coast of England, a classic holiday resort.

clue.text: Mixed drink for Myrtle or Rosemary, say

definitions.meaning: a drink of fruit juice and spirit or vinegar
myrtle and rosemary are both bushy plants

explanation.surface: Someone orders a cocktail for two women, Myrtle and Rosemary.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals make Myrtle and Rosemary look like women's names; they are plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Myrtle and rosemary are both woody bushes, and a shrub is also an old cordial of fruit and spirits.

clue.text: Shot producing bang?

parts.note: a cricket stroke, but read also as a haircut that gives a straight fringe, which Americans call bangs

explanation.walkthrough: A square cut is a cricket stroke played square of the wicket on the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: A square cut is a cricket stroke, and a fringe cut straight across would be a square cut too.

clue.text: Run into creatures, each found in Northern waters

indicators.note: into says the first piece goes inside the next

parts.note: beings are living creatures
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Animals of every kind are found swimming in Arctic seas.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bering Sea lies in the far north Pacific between Alaska and Siberia.

clue.text: Outcome of toss leading to sharp advantage, initially

indicators.note: leading to says the first piece comes before the second

parts.note: a coin toss lands heads or tails
tart means sharp in taste

explanation.surface: Winning the toss gives a team a sharp early edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A head start is an advantage held at the beginning of a race or contest.

clue.text: Mechanic extracting some part if ice recedes

indicators.note: extracting some says the answer is pulled out as a run of letters inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A mechanic takes some part out if the ice melts back.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'Mechanic extracting' doesn't stand in for the answer; 'extracting' belongs with 'some' as the signal to lift letters out.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificer is a skilled craftsman or military mechanic.

clue.text: Not a painter's top work

parts.note: not a masterpiece, but read literally a layer the decorator applies beneath the final coat

explanation.definitionFit: An undercoat is the layer of paint laid down before the final top coat.

clue.text: A bit of a bloomer made by Penny and others

parts.note: et al is Latin shorthand for and others

explanation.surface: Penny and her friends make a small blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder; it is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A petal is one part of a flower, and a bloomer is a flowering plant.

clue.text: Artist making live appearance in series

indicators.note: appearance in says the first piece shows up inside the second

parts.note: runs are series, as of wins or performances
to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: A performer makes a live appearance in a television series.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Paul Rubens was a Flemish Baroque painter, so he is an artist.

clue.text: Like brass that's squandered

definitions.meaning: brass instruments are played by blowing

explanation.surface: Money, or brass, that has been wasted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brass' is also British slang for money, which makes the surface about waste.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass instruments are sounded by breath, and blowing money means spending it wastefully.

clue.text: For rich, I could be so frightful

indicators.note: could be says these letters might be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Someone muses that, for the wealthy, they could be terribly frightening.
explanation.definitionFit: Horrific means causing horror, which makes it a close synonym of frightful.

clue.text: Stony girl's heartless sport

indicators.note: heartless says the central letter of the word is taken out

parts.note: rugby is a sport

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted girl plays a heartless game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stony girl' is a girl's name that is also a stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruby is a girl's name and also a precious red gemstone, so the girl is stony.

clue.text: Shrewd woman replacing it in city

indicators.note: replacing says one piece takes the place of another within the word

parts.note: taken as written
Ann is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A clever woman takes over from someone in the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Canny means shrewd and careful, especially with money.

clue.text: Foreigner that is not reaching conclusions

indicators.note: not reaching conclusions says each word stops short, losing its final letter

explanation.surface: A foreigner who never gets to the point of what they say.
explanation.definitionFit: A Thai is a native of Thailand, who is a foreigner to a British reader.

clue.text: Go over border river and burn bridges

definitions.meaning: Caesar crossed the river marking the border of Roman Italy
commit oneself irrevocably with no way back

explanation.surface: An army fords a frontier river and destroys the bridges behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar literally forded that frontier river in 49 BC, and the phrase now means taking an irrevocable step.

clue.text: Cause of frustration — I translate badly

indicators.note: badly says the letters are put in a poor, jumbled order

explanation.surface: Someone admits their poor translation is a source of annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: A tantaliser teases by holding out something just out of reach, which causes frustration.

clue.text: English poet, dull for Americans

definitions.meaning: Thomas ... wrote the Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard
grey, meaning dull or overcast, in American spelling

explanation.surface: An English poet is thought boring in the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Gray was an English poet, and gray is the US spelling of grey, meaning drab.
